prerequisites: Lesson 1 — declare an origin and a positive direction before assigning signed positions; distance vs. signed displacement $\Delta x = x_f - x_i$.
Read a value off a labelled axis and calculate the slope of a straight line as rise over run (BASIS Physics 8 Unit 1).
majorObjective: Read position and displacement from a position-time graph, calculate velocity as its slope, and match the shape of a position-time graph to a verbal description of the motion.
subObjectives: Read the position of an object at a stated time, and the displacement between two times, directly from an $x$-$t$ graph.
Decide from a description of a motion whether the object has been displaced and in which direction.
Calculate velocity as the slope $v = \dfrac{\Delta x}{\Delta t}$ of a straight segment, with a sign and a unit.
Select the correctly shaped $x$-$t$ graph for a description of the motion, using slope sign for direction and steepness for speed.

hook.prompt: On a position-time graph, an object's curve is a horizontal line for 4 s. What is the object doing during those 4 seconds?
choices: Moving at a constant, non-zero velocity.
Staying at one position — its velocity is zero.
Speeding up, because the line is flat.

priorKnowledge: Position $x$ is a signed location in a declared frame. This lesson reads $x$ as the vertical quantity on a graph whose horizontal quantity is time $t$, and treats the slope $\Delta x / \Delta t$ as the velocity.

chunks.title: Reading position and displacement from the graph
chunks.concept: A **position-time graph** plots signed position $x$ on the vertical axis against time $t$ on the horizontal axis. To read the position at a time, go up from that time to the curve, then across to the $x$-axis. The **displacement** between two times is the signed change in the height of the curve: $$\Delta x = x_f - x_i$$ Reading up from a later time and subtracting the earlier position gives both the size and the direction of the displacement. The graph shows position, not the path — a flat section means the object held its position, not that it vanished.
chunks.representation:
Work in a fixed order:

1. Read $x_i$ — the curve's height at the earlier time.
2. Read $x_f$ — the curve's height at the later time.
3. Subtract: $\Delta x = x_f - x_i$, keeping the sign.
4. State the direction the sign encodes in the declared frame.

conceptFigures.caption: A three-stage journey: constant-velocity climb from +1 m to +7 m, a pause at +7 m, then a return to +1 m. Each labelled point is an ordered pair (time, position).

workedExample.problem: Using the graph above, find (a) the object's position at $t = 4\ \mathrm{s}$ and (b) its displacement between $t = 1\ \mathrm{s}$ and $t = 8\ \mathrm{s}$.

phases.label: Read the position at t = 4 s
steps: At $t = 4\ \mathrm{s}$ the curve is on the flat section between $t = 3\ \mathrm{s}$ and $t = 5\ \mathrm{s}$.
Read across to the axis: $x = +7\ \mathrm{m}$.

phases.label: Read the two endpoint positions
steps: At $t = 1\ \mathrm{s}$ the curve is on the first sloped section, one-third of the way up: $x_i = +3\ \mathrm{m}$.
At $t = 8\ \mathrm{s}$ the curve has returned to its lowest labelled point: $x_f = +1\ \mathrm{m}$.

phases.label: Subtract for the displacement
steps: $\Delta x = x_f - x_i = (+1\ \mathrm{m}) - (+3\ \mathrm{m}) = -2\ \mathrm{m}$.
The negative sign means the object finished 2 m in the negative direction from where it was at $t = 1\ \mathrm{s}$, even though it went far in the positive direction in between.

workedExample.keyMove: Displacement is a difference of two heights on the curve, not the length of the wiggle between them.

formativeCheck.question: On the journey graph above, what is the object's displacement between $t = 0\ \mathrm{s}$ and $t = 3\ \mathrm{s}$?

incorrect.1: $+7\ \mathrm{m}$ is the final position $x_f$, not the change in position. Subtract the starting position.
incorrect.2: $+8\ \mathrm{m}$ would be the answer if the object started at the origin; here it started at $+1\ \mathrm{m}$.
incorrect.3: The curve is at two different heights at $t = 0$ and $t = 3\ \mathrm{s}$, so the displacement is not zero. A zero displacement needs equal heights.

hint: Displacement is $\Delta x = x_f - x_i$. Read the height of the curve at $t = 3\ \mathrm{s}$ and at $t = 0\ \mathrm{s}$, then subtract.
formativeCheck.solution: At $t = 0\ \mathrm{s}$ the curve is at $x_i = +1\ \mathrm{m}$. At $t = 3\ \mathrm{s}$ it has climbed to $x_f = +7\ \mathrm{m}$. The displacement is $\Delta x = x_f - x_i = (+7\ \mathrm{m}) - (+1\ \mathrm{m}) = +6\ \mathrm{m}$.

chunks.title: Slope of a position-time graph is velocity
chunks.concept: For a straight segment of a position-time graph, the **slope** is the velocity: $$v = \frac{\Delta x}{\Delta t} = \frac{x_2 - x_1}{t_2 - t_1}$$ The unit is metres per second, from position units divided by time units. The **sign** of the slope is the direction of motion in the declared frame: a line going up to the right is positive velocity, a line going down to the right is negative velocity, and a flat line is zero velocity. The **steepness** is the speed: a steeper line means a larger distance covered per second.
chunks.representation:
Pick two points on the same straight segment.

1. Take the rise $\Delta x = x_2 - x_1$, keeping its sign.
2. Take the run $\Delta t = t_2 - t_1$ — always positive, since time only increases.
3. Divide, and attach the unit m/s.

conceptFigures.caption: Two straight segments with their slope triangles. Segment 1: Δx = +8 m over Δt = 2 s gives v = +4 m/s. Segment 2: Δx = −6 m over Δt = 3 s gives v = −2 m/s.

workedExample.problem: From the two-segment graph above, find the velocity on each segment and say which motion is faster.

phases.label: Segment 1 — read the two points
steps: The segment runs from $(0\ \mathrm{s},\ 0\ \mathrm{m})$ to $(2\ \mathrm{s},\ +8\ \mathrm{m})$.
$\Delta x = (+8\ \mathrm{m}) - (0\ \mathrm{m}) = +8\ \mathrm{m}$;  $\Delta t = 2\ \mathrm{s} - 0\ \mathrm{s} = 2\ \mathrm{s}$.

phases.label: Segment 1 — divide
steps: $v_1 = \dfrac{\Delta x}{\Delta t} = \dfrac{+8\ \mathrm{m}}{2\ \mathrm{s}} = +4\ \mathrm{m/s}$.
Positive: the object moves in the positive direction at $4\ \mathrm{m/s}$.

phases.label: Segment 2 — read, then divide
steps: From $(2\ \mathrm{s},\ +8\ \mathrm{m})$ to $(5\ \mathrm{s},\ +2\ \mathrm{m})$: $\Delta x = (+2\ \mathrm{m}) - (+8\ \mathrm{m}) = -6\ \mathrm{m}$, $\Delta t = 3\ \mathrm{s}$.
$v_2 = \dfrac{-6\ \mathrm{m}}{3\ \mathrm{s}} = -2\ \mathrm{m/s}$ — motion in the negative direction.

phases.label: Compare the speeds
steps: Speed is the size of the velocity: $|v_1| = 4\ \mathrm{m/s}$ versus $|v_2| = 2\ \mathrm{m/s}$.
Segment 1 is faster, which is why its line is steeper.

workedExample.keyMove: Keep the sign on the rise; the run is always positive because time only moves forward.

formativeCheck.question: Take north as positive. A position-time graph is a straight line from $(2\ \mathrm{s},\ +10\ \mathrm{m})$ to $(6\ \mathrm{s},\ +2\ \mathrm{m})$. What is the velocity?

feedback.correct: Correct — $\Delta x = 2 - 10 = -8\ \mathrm{m}$, $\Delta t = 6 - 2 = 4\ \mathrm{s}$, so $v = -8/4 = -2\ \mathrm{m/s}$ (2 m/s south).

incorrect.0: The height of the curve decreases as time goes forward, so the slope — and the velocity — must be negative.
incorrect.2: Check the run: $\Delta t = 6 - 2 = 4\ \mathrm{s}$, not 3 s or 2.67 s. $-8\ \mathrm{m} \div 4\ \mathrm{s} = -2\ \mathrm{m/s}$.
incorrect.3: $8\ \mathrm{m}$ is the size of $\Delta x$ alone. Velocity is $\Delta x$ divided by $\Delta t$, and the sign is negative here.

hint: $v = \dfrac{x_2 - x_1}{t_2 - t_1}$. Put the later point second in both the top and the bottom.
The position drops from $+10\ \mathrm{m}$ to $+2\ \mathrm{m}$ while time rises from 2 s to 6 s — expect a negative answer.
formativeCheck.solution: $\Delta x = x_2 - x_1 = (+2\ \mathrm{m}) - (+10\ \mathrm{m}) = -8\ \mathrm{m}$. $\Delta t = t_2 - t_1 = 6\ \mathrm{s} - 2\ \mathrm{s} = 4\ \mathrm{s}$. $v = \dfrac{-8\ \mathrm{m}}{4\ \mathrm{s}} = -2\ \mathrm{m/s}$, i.e. 2 m/s in the negative (south) direction.

chunks.title: Matching the graph shape to the motion
chunks.concept:
Because slope is velocity, the **shape** of a position-time graph reports the motion directly:

- **At rest** → a horizontal line (zero slope).
- **Constant velocity in the positive direction** → a straight line sloping up to the right.
- **Constant velocity in the negative direction** → a straight line sloping down to the right.
- **Faster constant speed** → a steeper straight line (in whichever direction).

A description of a motion can be turned into the right graph by asking, in order: is it moving? which direction? how fast compared with other parts?
chunks.representation:
Translate the words to slope features:

- “stays” / “parked” / “held still” → flat.
- “moves forward” / “away in the + direction” → slope up.
- “moves back” / “returns” / “in the − direction” → slope down.
- “faster” → steeper; “slower” → shallower.

conceptFigures.caption: Four straight-line position-time graphs. A: horizontal (at rest). B: gentle upward slope (slow, positive velocity). C: downward slope (negative velocity). D: steep upward slope (fast, positive velocity).

workedExample.problem: A drone hovers in place, then flies quickly away from its pilot in the positive direction at a steady speed. Which of graphs A–D matches the second stage, and why not the others?

phases.label: Name the motion of the second stage
steps: “Flies away in the positive direction” → position increases, so the slope is positive.
“Quickly … at a steady speed” → a straight line, and a steep one.

phases.label: Test each option
steps: A is horizontal — that is the hovering stage, not the flight.
C slopes down — that would be flying back toward the pilot.
B slopes up but only gently — that is a slow departure, not a quick one.

phases.label: Choose
steps: D — a steep upward straight line — is the steady, fast departure in the positive direction.

workedExample.keyMove: Decide direction from the sign of the slope first, then speed from the steepness.

formativeCheck.question: Take east as positive. A car drives west at a constant speed for the whole trip. Which position-time graph shape is correct?
choices: A straight line sloping up to the right.
A straight line sloping down to the right.
A curve that gets steeper to the right.

feedback.correct: Correct — west is the negative direction, so position decreases steadily and the line slopes down to the right at a constant rate.

incorrect.0: A horizontal line is zero velocity — the car is not moving. This car is moving the whole time.
incorrect.1: An upward slope is positive velocity, i.e. moving east. This car moves west.
incorrect.3: A curve that steepens means the speed is changing. The car's speed is constant, so the graph is a straight line.

hint: West is negative in an east-positive frame, so the position becomes more negative as time goes on.
Constant speed → straight line; direction → sign of the slope.
formativeCheck.solution: In an east-positive frame, driving west means the position decreases as time increases, so the slope is negative — a line sloping down to the right. The speed is constant, so the line is straight, not curved.

misconceptions.question: Two objects are shown on the same position-time graph. At $t = 5\ \mathrm{s}$, object P's curve is higher than object Q's curve, but object Q's curve is steeper. Which object is moving faster at that moment?
choices: Object P, because its curve is higher.
Object Q, because its curve is steeper.
They move at the same speed because they are on the same graph.
Object P, because a higher position always means a higher speed.

feedback.correct: Correct — speed is read from the slope, not the height. A steeper curve means a larger change in position per second.

incorrect.0: Height on a position-time graph is position, not speed. Being farther from the origin does not mean moving faster.
incorrect.2: Sharing a graph says nothing about the speeds — each curve has its own slope.
incorrect.3: Position and speed are different quantities. A parked car far from the origin has a high position and zero speed.

hint: On a position-time graph, what does the vertical height tell you? What does the slope tell you?
Speed is a rate of change of position, so it lives in the slope.
misconceptions.solution: On a position-time graph the height is the position and the slope is the velocity. Object Q's curve is steeper, so its position changes faster — object Q is moving faster, regardless of which curve is higher at that instant.

errorAnalysis.studentWork:
Problem: Take up as positive. A lift's position-time graph is a straight line from $(0\ \mathrm{s},\ +12\ \mathrm{m})$ to $(4\ \mathrm{s},\ +4\ \mathrm{m})$. Find the velocity.

Student's response: “The change in position is $12 + 4 = 16\ \mathrm{m}$. The time is $4\ \mathrm{s}$. So $v = 16 / 4 = +4\ \mathrm{m/s}$ upward.”
prompts: State the rule the student should have used for $\Delta x$.
Identify the first step that is not supported by that rule.
Repair the response: give the correct velocity with sign and direction, and verify it against the graph.
errorAnalysis.modelResponse: The rule is $\Delta x = x_f - x_i$ — a subtraction, keeping signs. The first unsupported step is “$12 + 4 = 16\ \mathrm{m}$”: the student added the two positions instead of subtracting them, which also loses the direction information. Correct: $\Delta x = x_f - x_i = (+4\ \mathrm{m}) - (+12\ \mathrm{m}) = -8\ \mathrm{m}$; $\Delta t = 4\ \mathrm{s} - 0\ \mathrm{s} = 4\ \mathrm{s}$; $v = \dfrac{-8\ \mathrm{m}}{4\ \mathrm{s}} = -2\ \mathrm{m/s}$, i.e. 2 m/s downward. Verify against the graph: the line goes down to the right, so the slope is negative, which matches a downward (negative) velocity.

representationConnections: A verbal description fixes the direction and steadiness of the motion; that becomes a slope sign and a slope steepness; the slope is the velocity in m/s; and the heights of the curve at two times give the displacement. The same motion must read the same way in words, on the graph, and in the velocity calculation.

lessonAssessment.question: A position-time graph is a straight line from $(1\ \mathrm{s},\ -3\ \mathrm{m})$ to $(5\ \mathrm{s},\ +9\ \mathrm{m})$. Which statement is fully correct?

incorrect.1: The displacement is $x_f - x_i = (+9\ \mathrm{m}) - (-3\ \mathrm{m}) = +12\ \mathrm{m}$; subtracting a negative adds. The velocity value is right but the displacement is not.
incorrect.2: Velocity is displacement divided by the time interval $\Delta t = 4\ \mathrm{s}$, not the displacement itself.
incorrect.3: The curve rises from $-3\ \mathrm{m}$ to $+9\ \mathrm{m}$ as time goes forward, so both the displacement and the velocity are positive.

hint: Displacement: $x_f - x_i = (+9\ \mathrm{m}) - (-3\ \mathrm{m})$. Watch the double negative.
Velocity: divide that displacement by $\Delta t = 5\ \mathrm{s} - 1\ \mathrm{s}$.

lessonAssessment.question: A cyclist rolls forward (positive direction) at a steady speed, stops at a light for a while, then rolls forward again at a slower steady speed. Which sequence of position-time segments matches this story?
choices: Up-sloping line, then flat line, then a less steep up-sloping line.
Up-sloping line, then flat line, then a steeper up-sloping line.
Flat line, then up-sloping line, then down-sloping line.
Up-sloping line, then down-sloping line, then flat line.

feedback.correct: Correct — forward at a steady speed is a straight up-slope, the stop is a flat section, and the slower second ride is a shallower up-slope.

incorrect.1: A steeper second up-slope would mean the cyclist sped up. The story says the second ride is slower, so the slope must be shallower.
incorrect.2: Starting flat would mean the cyclist was stopped at the start, but the story begins with rolling forward.
incorrect.3: A down-sloping section is motion in the negative direction. The cyclist never rides backward in this story.

hint: Translate each phase: steady forward → straight up-slope; stopped → flat; slower forward → shallower up-slope.
Direction sets the sign of the slope; speed sets the steepness.
lessonAssessment.solution: Rolling forward at a steady speed is a straight line sloping up. Stopping is a flat (zero-slope) section. Rolling forward again but slower is another upward line, less steep than the first because the speed is lower. That is the first option.

lessonAssessment.scenario:
Take east as positive. A delivery robot's motion is recorded as a position-time graph made of three straight segments:

| Segment | Start (t, x) | End (t, x) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | (0 s, +2 m) | (4 s, +14 m) |
| 2 | (4 s, +14 m) | (7 s, +14 m) |
| 3 | (7 s, +14 m) | (10 s, +5 m) |

parts.prompt: (a) Find the robot's velocity on each of the three segments. Show $\Delta x$, $\Delta t$, and the sign for each.
parts.modelResponse: Segment 1: $\Delta x = (+14) - (+2) = +12\ \mathrm{m}$, $\Delta t = 4\ \mathrm{s}$, $v_1 = +12/4 = +3\ \mathrm{m/s}$ (east). Segment 2: $\Delta x = (+14) - (+14) = 0\ \mathrm{m}$, $\Delta t = 3\ \mathrm{s}$, $v_2 = 0\ \mathrm{m/s}$ (at rest). Segment 3: $\Delta x = (+5) - (+14) = -9\ \mathrm{m}$, $\Delta t = 3\ \mathrm{s}$, $v_3 = -9/3 = -3\ \mathrm{m/s}$ (west).

parts.prompt: (b) Find the robot's total displacement over the whole 10 s, and state its direction.
parts.modelResponse: Displacement uses only the first and last points: $\Delta x = x_f - x_i = (+5\ \mathrm{m}) - (+2\ \mathrm{m}) = +3\ \mathrm{m}$, i.e. 3 m east.

parts.prompt: (c) A student says “the robot's speed on segment 1 and segment 3 is the same, so those segments look identical on the graph.” Evaluate this claim.
parts.modelResponse: The speeds are equal in size ($|{+3}| = |{-3}| = 3\ \mathrm{m/s}$), so the two segments have equally steep lines. But the velocities have opposite signs: segment 1 slopes up to the right (moving east) and segment 3 slopes down to the right (moving west). The segments are mirror images in steepness, not identical — the slope directions are opposite.

examConnection: Every later kinematics representation is read the same way: slope is a rate, area is an accumulation, and height is the plotted quantity. Matching a described motion to the right graph and extracting a signed rate from a slope are recurring AP and IB Paper 1 tasks.
summary: On a position-time graph, height is position and slope is velocity. Read displacement as $\Delta x = x_f - x_i$ from the curve's heights at two times. Compute velocity as $v = \Delta x / \Delta t$ on a straight segment, keeping the sign for direction. Match a described motion to a shape by fixing direction from the slope's sign and speed from its steepness; a flat line is at rest, a straight sloped line is constant velocity, and a steeper line is faster.

exitQuestion.question: A position-time graph curve passes through $(2\ \mathrm{s},\ +6\ \mathrm{m})$ and $(6\ \mathrm{s},\ +6\ \mathrm{m})$. Between those two times the curve dips down to $+1\ \mathrm{m}$ and comes back. What is the displacement from $t = 2\ \mathrm{s}$ to $t = 6\ \mathrm{s}$?

feedback.correct: Correct — displacement compares only the endpoints, and the curve is at the same height $+6\ \mathrm{m}$ at both times, so $\Delta x = 0$.

incorrect.1: $-5\ \mathrm{m}$ is how far down the dip goes, not the endpoint-to-endpoint change. Displacement ignores what happens in between.
incorrect.2: $+10\ \mathrm{m}$ looks like a distance built from the trip down and back up. Displacement is not path length.
incorrect.3: $+6\ \mathrm{m}$ is the position at each endpoint, not the change in position.

hint: Displacement is $x_f - x_i$ — only the two endpoint heights matter.
The curve starts and ends at the same height.
exitQuestion.solution: Displacement depends only on the initial and final positions: $x_i = +6\ \mathrm{m}$ at $t = 2\ \mathrm{s}$ and $x_f = +6\ \mathrm{m}$ at $t = 6\ \mathrm{s}$. $\Delta x = x_f - x_i = 0\ \mathrm{m}$. The dip changes the distance travelled but not the displacement.
